q: In the label-pipeline-rebuild project, what do we know about q-lbl-churn-window?
a: It asks which inactivity window defines churn in cards.churn_labels. The 60-day rule gave 7.9 percent churn on 2025-H1 snapshots and 90 days gave 6.1 percent. The answer is now 90 days plus closure within 120 days (dec-lbl-churn-closure).

q: In the label-pipeline-rebuild project, what came of exp-405, the fraud model comparison?
a: lbl-fraud-gbm-v4 on rebuilt labels reached recall 0.58 at 1 percent alerts against 0.52 for lbl-fraud-gbm-v3 on lbl-oot-2025h2. That led to fnd-fraud-v4-lift and to dec-lbl-promote-fraud-v4.

q: In the label-pipeline-rebuild project, what does lbl-fraud-gbm-v4 depend on for its labels?
a: It trains on cards.fraud_labels built with feat-lbl-fraud-flag-v2, which covers categories A and B, and it is evaluated only on transactions with 120 days of label maturity (fnd-fraud-maturity).

q: In the label-pipeline-rebuild project, what is the current churn label definition?
a: Churn is no approved transaction for 90 days, or an account closure within 120 days of the snapshot (dec-lbl-churn-closure), implemented as feat-lbl-churn-flag-closure. It replaced the 90-day-only rule in dec-lbl-churn-90d.

q: In the label-pipeline-rebuild project, what is the rebuilt churn rate on 2025-H1 snapshots, and what did the legacy 60-day rule give?
a: 6.4 percent on the 4.6M account-snapshots under the rebuilt closure-inclusive definition (fnd-churn-rate-rebuilt). The legacy 60-day rule gave 7.9 percent (exp-401).

q: In the label-pipeline-rebuild project, why did we include friendly-fraud disputes in the fraud label?
a: Category B raised the fraud label rate from 0.41 to 0.47 percent of approved transactions on 2025-Q2 (exp-403), and fraud-ops books those disputes as loss. dec-lbl-friendly-fraud added them so the label matches loss.
